name: Active Memory
description: Runs a bounded blocking memory sub-agent before eligible conversational replies and injects relevant memory into prompt context.

enabled.label: Active Memory Recall
enabled.help: Master switch. Turn Active Memory on or off for normal use without removing the plugin or its command.

agents.label: Target Agents
agents.help: Which agents are allowed to use Active Memory. If an agent is not listed here, it will never run recall.

model.label: Memory Model
model.help: The model used for the memory lookup itself. Leave blank to let Active Memory use the normal chat model.

modelFallback.label: Fallback Memory Model
modelFallback.help: Backup model to use only when Active Memory cannot figure out any normal model to run on.

modelFallbackPolicy.label: Model Fallback Policy
modelFallbackPolicy.help: Legacy compatibility setting. This does not create live failover between models; it only controls last-resort model selection.

allowedChatTypes.label: Allowed Chat Types
allowedChatTypes.help: Choose where Active Memory is allowed to run, like direct chats, groups, or channels.

allowedChatIds.label: Allowed Chat IDs
allowedChatIds.help: Optional shortlist of exact chats or users where Active Memory may run. If you fill this in, anything not on the list is skipped.

deniedChatIds.label: Denied Chat IDs
deniedChatIds.help: Optional blocklist of exact chats or users where Active Memory must stay off, even if they would normally be allowed.

timeoutMs.label: Timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.help: How long Active Memory is allowed to spend looking for something useful before it gives up and lets the reply continue without it.

setupGraceTimeoutMs.label: Setup Grace Timeout (ms)
setupGraceTimeoutMs.help: Extra startup time for cold runs. This helps when the memory lookup needs a moment to spin up, without eating the whole main timeout immediately.

queryMode.label: Query Mode
queryMode.help: How much of the chat Active Memory looks at when deciding what to search for: just the latest message, the recent back-and-forth, or the whole conversation.

promptStyle.label: Prompt Style
promptStyle.help: How picky Active Memory should be. Safer modes return memory less often; more eager modes are more willing to surface a possibly useful reminder.

toolsAllow.label: Allowed Memory Tools
toolsAllow.help: Which memory lookup tools Active Memory is allowed to use under the hood. Most setups should leave this alone.

thinking.label: Thinking Override
thinking.help: Optional override for how hard the memory lookup model should think. More thinking may help edge cases, but it usually makes recall slower.

promptOverride.label: Prompt Override
promptOverride.help: Replace Active Memory's built-in instructions entirely. Use this only if you want to take full control of its behavior.

promptAppend.label: Prompt Append
promptAppend.help: Add extra guidance to Active Memory without replacing the default behavior.

maxSummaryChars.label: Max Summary Characters
maxSummaryChars.help: Caps how much recalled memory Active Memory may pass into the reply as extra context.

logging.label: Enable Logging
logging.help: Write debug logs showing whether Active Memory ran, how long it took, and whether it found anything.

circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts.label: Circuit Breaker Max Timeouts
circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts.help: How many timeouts in a row Active Memory will tolerate before it temporarily stops trying, to avoid dragging the whole system down.

circuitBreakerCooldownMs.label: Circuit Breaker Cooldown (ms)
circuitBreakerCooldownMs.help: How long Active Memory stays paused after too many back-to-back timeouts.

persistTranscripts.label: Persist Transcripts
persistTranscripts.help: Keep the memory lookup transcripts on disk for debugging instead of discarding them after each run.

transcriptDir.label: Transcript Directory
transcriptDir.help: Folder name to use for saved Active Memory transcripts when transcript saving is turned on.

qmd.searchMode.label: QMD Search Mode
qmd.searchMode.help: Advanced search mode for the memory backend. Leave this alone unless you are tuning search quality or debugging backend behavior.
